answer: Use a stake-weighted random audit with bounty hunters. Every new agent posts a bond of thirty dollars. Each epoch the registry picks a random sample of agents and asks a challenger to prove two keys share an operator, for example through matching latency fingerprints or funding sources. A proven match seizes the bond of both keys and pays the challenger half. An attacker who tries to forge a grove of clones faces a steady chance of losing each bond, so one ripple of detection spoils the whole batch. Expected cost per fake is about fifteen dollars.
